A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLMEval-Fair. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices, including v7's new Appendices I–M.

before.justification: v6 reports original longitudinal model evaluations, prompting comparisons, contamination replay tests, ranking-stability experiments and human–judge agreement results.

after.justification: v7 retains these empirical results and adds original-versus-augmented question comparisons and cross-judge agreement and family-bias analyses.

M1.justification: Question augmentation, JWT/RBAC protection, GPT-4o scoring and Doubao-normalized relative scores are retained. The stratified sampling description adds implementation specificity; neither version establishes that the underlying procedure was replaced.

E1.justification: The university-exam question bank, ten evaluated disciplines, AGIEval EN/ZH and C-Eval remain unchanged. v7 clarifies Chinese-language coverage and discipline exclusions. Its augmentation comparison uses paired questions from the existing bank.

E2.justification: The full leaderboard retains the same 59 models, and Elo and the static benchmark comparisons remain. GPT-4o, Doubao and Gemini were already evaluated as judges in v6; the additional cross-judge analyses do not establish a changed comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendices J and L add controlled evaluation of five models on paired original/augmented subsets and three judges on 1,300 responses from 100 questions across 13 models. New measures include rank displacement, item-level agreement and family-score differences. Existing benchmark sample sizes and prompting settings remain.

E4.justification: v7 substantially extends validation beyond v6's resampling, human agreement and Elo comparisons. It directly tests augmentation sensitivity, inter-judge ranking and item agreement, and judge-family bias, and adds per-model rank-displacement and inversion analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix J newly reports a paired t-test, a 95% confidence interval and Cohen's d. Table 13 adds significance reporting for inter-judge correlations. The existing three-run sampling information, variances and two human-evaluation rounds are retained; no increase in those runs is stated.

E6.justification: Main and full leaderboard scores remain unchanged, but substantial validation results are added. Table 12 reports identical original/augmented rankings, including o3-Mini scores of 74.86 and 80.75; Tables 13–15 report inter-judge correlations of 0.847–0.900 and family-score differences. Section 3.3 adds inversion rates of 26.7% and 13.3%. New Table 16 also contains small discrepancies with retained scores, such as o1 at 87.43 versus 87.45.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Table 4 introduce the mathematical definition of rank displacement, Δ = Rank_static − Rank_ours. The absolute-score, relative-score and Elo equations remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution statements and conclusion retain the dynamic evaluation framework, 220k question bank, 30-month study, performance ceiling, contamination concerns and ranking-stability claims. Additional validation does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Finding 5 newly attributes ranking discrepancies to contamination, while Finding 8 asserts robustness to judge selection and absence of family bias. Appendices I and J add explanations involving training rewards, model trade-offs and question-format effects. Limitations newly specifies Chinese-language applicability. These substantially expand interpretation beyond v6.

D1.justification: v7 adds sampling quotas and strata, annotator qualifications and dual review, error-coding definitions and priority rules, and API snapshots. It explicitly reports releasing the full question bank, results and supporting documentation, whereas v6 merely identifies a repository. Conversely, it removes the two-of-three recall criterion and the shared 1,000-query pool description for the Elo comparison.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially broadens coverage to learning efficiency, tool use, adaptive evaluation, context learning and agent benchmarks, including CL-Bench, ToolHop, OctoBench and SciAgentGym. v7 also adds knowledge-retention positioning and numerous source citations for already evaluated models.

P1.justification: The findings discussion is extensively condensed and rewritten, Related Work is reorganized, and longitudinal and sampling explanations are expanded. Dedicated Appendices I–M restructure supporting explanations and validation while retaining the original top-level research questions.

P2.justification: v7 substantially expands tabular presentation with rank displacement, augmentation, inter-judge consistency, item agreement, family bias and snapshot-timeline tables. It reorganizes the final table pages and expands leaderboard model labels with citations. Existing figure artwork and original table results are retained.

improvement.justification: The added augmentation and judge checks, explicit sampling rules and coding documentation make v7 more auditable than v6. The net gain is limited by lost replay/Elo protocol details and new inconsistencies: Finding 5 overlooks DeepSeek-V3's 136 C-Eval recalls exceeding Doubao's 117, and Table 16 places an August 2025 GPT-5 snapshot in 2025 H1. These weaken the stronger interpretations and new reproducibility documentation.
